verdicts.correction: The program is not conforming source, so under the spec there is no expected stdout. `INVOKE L1C08EOC "NEW" RETURNING E` violates §14.9.23.3 SR3 ("The value of literal-1 shall be the name of a method defined in the factory interface of object-class-name-1"). `CLASS-ID. L1C08EOC.` has no INHERITS clause, so it inherits nothing (§11.3.4 GR2, §9.3.9) and its factory interface has no New method. New is defined only by BASE (§16.2 BaseFactoryInterface), and the spec has no rule that makes BASE inheritance implicit. The golden depends on the compiler's non-ISO behavior that every class has NEW. Fix: declare `CLASS-ID. L1C08EOC INHERITS FROM BASE.` with its own `REPOSITORY. CLASS BASE.` (§11.3.3 SR2). The compiler currently refuses this with COBOLNET0821 'INHERITS FROM BASE: no such a class is defined in this compilation group', which is a compiler defect (BASE §16.2 not provided) and needs a kb/Work note. The expected lines START-NULL/DECL-SAME/AFTER-SAME/SUB-SAME/NAMED-NULL/SUB-NULL are correctly derived and should stay once the source is legal. Existing goldens have the same flaw (l1_exit_raising_object_sending CL1ERR, oo_ec_raise_object).

Same program as GR1 and the same defect: `INVOKE L1C08EOC "NEW"` on a class with no INHERITS FROM BASE breaks §14.9.23.3 SR3, so the source is illegal and no stdout can be derived from the spec. Once the class is `INHERITS FROM BASE` and the compiler supports BASE, the SUB-SAME/SUB-NULL derivation is sound. It is a real cross-program witness that separates one register per run unit from per-program registers.

all_upheld_flag: Not all upheld: both EXCEPTION-OBJECT rows are overturned because the source is illegal (NEW on a class that does not inherit from BASE, §14.9.23.3 SR3). I confirmed there is no implicit BASE inheritance anywhere in the spec (§9.3.9, §11.3.4, §16.2), and a corrected INHERITS FROM BASE version fails in the compiler with COBOLNET0821. What I tried against the upheld goldens: (1) End marker: checked 85 legality of nested programs and a separate program after END PROGRAM. The D and E lines discriminate, because if END PROGRAM L1C08D did not close D, E would be nested in D and invisible to C (§8.4.6.3 1)). The F line alone does not discriminate. (2) Entry-name negatives: in fixed form the `*>` lines have `*` in column 7, so they are comment lines at 85 too. G/A is otherwise legal, and the generic COBOL0001 is acceptable for a single-word format slot. (3) Environment division: re-derived the DECIMAL-POINT IS COMMA edits (12,5 into Z9,99 gives 12,50; 3,25 into 99,99 gives 03,25). A READ without AT END is fine because the read succeeds. The negative is otherwise legal. FD without LABEL RECORDS at 85 follows the existing 85-golden convention. (4) Float: checked SET Format 15 (FLOAT-INFINITY without SIGN is positive, §14.9.39.4 GR33, so SIGN-POS=Y). Checked that the class/sign/same-usage-with-other-endianness exemptions are exempt and that K (FLOAT-BINARY-32), N, the relation and COMPUTE each raise. RESUME NEXT STATEMENT after a relation skips past END-IF (§14.9.33.4 2)a) and NOTE 1). The declarative's RESUME stops the fatal-path termination (14.6.13.1.3 5) NOTE 2). EXCEPTION-STATUS returns 31 characters padded with trailing spaces; the .out omits them, but CutRunner.Normalize TrimEnds each line, so this is harmless. At 2002 the compiler gates the endianness phrase, SET CONTENT and the float class conditions (2014+), which is consistent with the 2014 directory. (5) Indirect STOP RUN: considered overturning as does-not-exercise-rule, because STOP RUN kills the run unit whatever rule 2 says. Kept it because the realistic wrong implementation is a declarative dispatcher that swallows a nested run-unit termination as a normal completion, and that one would print DECL-END/AFTER-RAISE. (6) Nonfatal no-handler: re-derived STRING 8)a)/e) (T=ABCD, P=05, NOT ON OVERFLOW ignored). ST=EC-OVERFLOW-STRING is set only when checking is enabled (§14.6.13.1.1), and AFTER-RAISE/ST=EC-USER-GOON pin the rule-4 continuation. Citations: I ran cite.py --check on all of them and all OK. The writer's `14.9.42.4` check only passes with the GR6 text, which I checked separately. The §14.6.13.1.5 '2)' label covers the unnumbered paragraph after the rule-2 list; cite.py accepts it, but it is not literally rule 2.
